chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Amr, from Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Ammar, who said: Harun al-Rashid wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him):
Exhort me and be succinct. So he wrote to him: There is nothing that your eye sees except that it has an exhortation in it.

key_terms.عظني: I'zni - exhort me, give me counsel that moves the heart
key_terms.موعظة: Maw'izah - exhortation, admonition, a lesson that softens the heart

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam Musa al-Kadhim give to Harun al-Rashid?
ai.summary: This hadith records a remarkable exchange between the Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid and Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the seventh Imam whom al-Rashid would later imprison. When the caliph asked for a brief piece of advice, the Imam responded with a profound and concise statement: everything visible contains a lesson. This reflects the Imam's extraordinary ability to distill deep wisdom into minimal words. For the original audience, the irony was palpable -- al-Rashid sought counsel from the very Imam he would persecute.
